name: Electrical & Smart Home
tagline: Switches, sockets and the automation layer behind them
description: Switch plates are the most-touched hardware in a house and the easiest thing to get wrong at the end of a project. This section covers modular wiring devices by grade, then the smart-home layer — which has to be decided at first fix, not after the walls close.

materials.name: Modular switch
materials.blurb: Standard 1M/2M modules in a plate — the Indian baseline
materials.description: The modular system every Indian electrician works with: modules clipped into a grid plate and mounting box. Specify the plate range early — it dictates the box depth the site has to build in.

materials.name: Premium switch
materials.blurb: Metal, glass and matte plates that suit a designed interior
materials.description: Same electrical guts, far better plates: brushed steel, glass, matte black, wood. The cheapest way to stop a beautiful wall being spoiled by a builder-grade white rectangle.

materials.name: Smart switch
materials.blurb: Wi-Fi or Zigbee module controlled by app and voice
materials.description: Replaces the mechanical switch with a relay that also answers to a phone or voice assistant. Needs a neutral wire at the switch box — confirm it at first fix or the whole plan changes.

materials.name: Touch switch
materials.blurb: Capacitive glass panel with no moving parts
materials.description: A flat glass plate that responds to touch, usually with a backlit indicator. Looks superb in a hotel-style bedroom; check the night-time LED brightness before committing.

materials.name: USB socket
materials.blurb: Type-A and Type-C charging built into the plate
materials.description: Removes the adaptor from bedside and desk sockets. Specify PD-capable Type-C where laptops and phones will charge — 5 V-only ports already feel dated.

materials.name: HDMI socket
materials.blurb: In-wall AV outlet that keeps cables out of sight
materials.description: A wall plate carrying HDMI through to the media unit, so a wall-mounted TV has no visible lead. Run a conduit rather than burying the cable — HDMI standards keep changing.

materials.name: Data socket (RJ45)
materials.blurb: Structured cabling outlet for wired networking
materials.description: Cat 6 or Cat 6A outlets back to a central rack. Wi-Fi has not removed the need for wired points at TVs, access points and workstations — put them in while the walls are open.

materials.name: Dimmer
materials.blurb: Level control for dimmable lighting circuits
materials.description: Rotary, slide or smart dimmers that make one room serve several moods. The dimmer must match the driver — mismatched LED dimming is the most common cause of flicker complaints.

materials.name: MCB distribution board
materials.blurb: The consumer unit — circuit protection for the whole home
materials.description: Where every circuit begins and every fault stops. Specify an RCCB/RCBO for socket and wet-area circuits; it is the difference between a trip and an electrocution.

materials.name: Smart home hub
materials.blurb: The controller that ties lights, blinds, AV and sensors together
materials.description: A central hub speaking Zigbee, Z-Wave, Matter or a proprietary protocol. Choose the ecosystem before buying any device — retrofitting a second protocol later doubles the cost.

materials.name: Motorised curtain track
materials.blurb: App and remote-controlled curtain and blind drives
materials.description: A quiet motor on the track, wired to a point behind the pelmet. The power point has to exist before the false ceiling closes, which makes this a first-fix decision.

materials.name: Occupancy / motion sensor
materials.blurb: PIR or microwave sensor that switches lights automatically
materials.description: Corridors, wardrobes, utility rooms and bathrooms all work better on sensors. Match the detection pattern to the room shape, or the light will switch off while somebody is still standing there.
